_comment: ADVERSARIAL-for-greedy workload (realistic): two heavy perception nets -- YOLOv8n detection + DroNet collision -- are released together and each wants to SHARD WIDE (4 harts) to hit its deadline, which grabs all 8 harts at once. Meanwhile the hard-real-time MLP controller fires @100Hz (10ms deadline). GREEDY/EDF commits both wide shards immediately (no lookahead) -> all 8 harts busy ~0-46ms -> the control instances due at 10/20/30ms cannot find a free hart and MISS their deadlines. A GLOBAL solver (CP-SAT/MOSEK) STAGGERS the two wide perception shards -- or narrows one -- so a hart is always free for control, meeting every deadline. Same 8 harts, same nets; only the scheduling intelligence differs. This is the 'optimal genuinely beats greedy' regime, and it is realistic: a fast drone with two onboard perception nets contending with hard-real-time flight control is exactly this conflict.
